sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and router setup
sections.what: Loads the web tools, the database connection and the shared request and reply shapes, and creates the router that collects this file's routes.
sections.why: Likely reason: every route file in this folder follows the same pattern so the main app can attach them.
sections.watch_out: Other code expects the name router, so renaming it breaks how these routes are attached.

sections.name: run_calculation
sections.title: Scenario calculation placeholder
sections.what: Accepts a scenario id and returns a fixed success reply with two fixed number lists, not a real calculation.
sections.why: Likely reason: a placeholder while the calculation engine is not connected. The code comment says it would call the engine.
sections.watch_out: Do not treat its output as real model results until the placeholder is replaced.

summary: Provides a calculation endpoint that is meant to run the full model math for a scenario, but currently returns fixed placeholder numbers.
purpose: Give the frontend a place to request a scenario's results. At present it does not calculate anything.
why: Likely reason: a stub added so screens can be built before the real calculation engine is connected. The code comment says this.
how: The caller sends a scenario id. The route ignores the database session and returns that id with a success message and two fixed lists of revenue and net income.
inputs: A scenario id in the request body, checked against the request shape in the schemas file.
outputs: A reply with the scenario id, status success, a message saying the calculation completed, and fixed numbers for revenue and net income.
risks: The numbers look like real results but are invented. A user could make decisions based on them.
debug: If results look wrong, confirm whether the real calculation engine is wired in elsewhere. This route returns the same numbers for every scenario.
